the symmetry transformations in the Lorentz group, and in particular the Wigner rotation and Iwasawa decomposition, can be demonstrated in polarization optics.
the internal symmetry groups of the massive and massless particle are the same, and that the internal symmetry group of the photon is the same as that of the massive particle.

the application of the theory of group representations to polarization optics.

the internal space-time symmetry of a massive particle leads to a Wigner rotation and an Iwasawa decomposition for a massless particle, and these can be realized in optics laboratories by combining rotation, phase-shift and attenuation filters.
